primitives.name: Perceptual State Uniqueness
primitives.verbatim_quote: The perception is one state of mind or nothing—as I have already so often said.
primitives.assumptions: Psychic integration occurs as a singular cognitive event rather than a summation of independent components.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No known singularity; assumes continuous perceptual consciousness.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI conformal prediction via non-additive belief combination; models human cognition as a unified posterior distribution over sensory inputs.
layer2.telemetry: Neural multi-voxel pattern analysis (MVPA) of fMRI data, measuring the fidelity of reconstructed perceptual states from brain activity patterns.

primitives.name: Sensory vs Perceptual Contrast
primitives.verbatim_quote: In many cases it is easy to compare the psychic results of the sensational with those of the perceptive process.
primitives.assumptions: Sensation is raw input while perception involves contextual cognitive integration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when attentional focus disrupts the natural flow between sensation and perception.

layer2.mapping: Analogous to GSE state-transition mapping where "sensation" is raw observation and "perception" is belief-updated state estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Behavioral reaction time differences in tasks requiring pure sensory discrimination versus contextually integrated recognition.

primitives.name: Contextual Perceptual Shift
primitives.verbatim_quote: We then see a marked difference in the way in which the impressed portions of the object are felt, in consequence of being cognized along with the reproduced portion, in the higher state of mind.
primitives.assumptions: Cognitive reappraisal alters the felt quality of previously encountered stimuli.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Occurs when prior knowledge conflicts with current sensory evidence, leading to perceptual ambiguity.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI Bayesian updating where posterior beliefs reshape the likelihood of observed data.
layer2.telemetry: Electrophysiological mismatch negativity (MMN) responses to unexpected stimulus continuations based on learned context.

primitives.name: Linguistic Syllable Reinterpretation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Take the already-quoted catch, Pas de lieu Rhône que nous: one may read this over and over again without recognizing the sounds to be identical with those of the words paddle your own canoe.
primitives.assumptions: Phonetic identity remains constant while semantic assignment causes perceptual reorganization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Lexical competition leads to temporary perceptual bistability between alternative interpretations.

layer2.mapping: Similar to GSE action-value divergence where the same environmental state can trigger multiple distinct policies depending on internal state.
layer2.telemetry: Visual priming effects showing faster lexical decision times when phonetically similar but semantically unrelated words are presented as primes.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that perception is a singular, holistic cognitive event rather than a modular summation of separate processes. This non-additive integration manifests as "contextual perceptual shift", where the felt quality of sensory impressions depends on prior knowledge and linguistic context. The "linguistic syllable reinterpretation" example demonstrates how phonetic identity can remain invariant while semantic assignment triggers a complete restructuring of the perceptual field. These primitives fail to capture the temporal dynamics of active inference, where perception is driven by minimizing prediction error through hypothesis testing. They also neglect the role of embodied agency and motor affordances in shaping perceptual content.
